title: See You in the Next Life
text:
A beautiful Indian girl is lying on her deathbed, surrounded by her family, best friends, colleagues and neighbors. Don't worry, she's not dying young. She has lived her life well to see those wrinkles on her cheeks that some of us call the signs of getting old. She was in her 80s when she took her last breath.

And just like you'd expect in every cliché love story, there's one person who's missing on her funeral. But what makes this story interesting is that she knew he would not come and she blames no one for that, but herself.

I can still see the way he would look at her in college, like a totally, madly in love kind of a guy. He was totally opposite of her. Silent like a moon, wounded in her love that the whole world called him full of scars, but still, he was brightening her life.

He said he loved her, but she ignored. He said he cared, but she didn't believe him. He constantly texted; she never replied on time. He always called to see if she was okay, and she hung up. He asked her to stay with him for a little while, but she left, making excuses. Got a bus to board, got a class to attend, running late, parents are waiting.

Still, he never complained. She was rude, she was bitchy, she was full of attitude. He was a calm and composed dude. She knew how he stopped texting and calling, and he thought he'd already disturbed her a lot. It was true; she was indeed disturbed by his constant presence in her life. 'I need personal space God damn it,' those were her words.

No more texts, no more calls, never did he wish to meet her again or see her in the eye. A long silence all over, and in that moment, she missed him. Her heart wanted to call him up; it wanted to text, but her brain denied. 'Why should I take the first step?' Ego successfully killed another one of its victims.

It was her to push him away, but by the time she realized this, it was too late. She settled with this thought that he didn't love her anymore. He would've found another lucky woman. Her ego had burnt her to ashes. But never did she forget him. Nor did she forget the lesson she learned because of him.

And then one day, she found a ray of hope to meet him for the first time again. She tried to put on the best makeup, keeping her hair open as he liked. And as she got ready to meet him again, she felt that fierceness in her heart, careless fire that everyone talked about back in those days; it all came back with just a little thought of seeing him.

She reached his house; she met everyone with a smile on her face, but her heart and eyes were constantly trying to find him. She came out of the hall, unlocking her car to go back home, disappointed. And that's when a beautiful lady came to her with a cute little girl, calling her mumma.

'My brother always said that you'd come. It's nice to meet you. My little daughter has grown up having heard stories about you.'

'Why isn't he home, is he that busy?' she asked instantly, controlling her emotions.

All these years when she thought he ignored her, he was actually ignoring himself. One night when she hung up his call saying, 'God damn it, I need personal space, stop calling me anymore,' he decided that he'd leave her alone for a while. Months passed by, and he started to get mad at little things, angry at everyone and everything. He stopped using the phone, thinking he might call her at his weakest moments. He got into depression. Lost his calmness, politeness; he grew mad.

And then one day, he changed. He found his calmness back. He started drinking and smoking. They kept him in control, emotionally and mentally. One night when he came back from the office, he was numb. The next morning, he didn't wake up. The hospital reports said he had eaten at least 50 pills that night. Maybe it was one of those nights when memories of someone don't let you sleep.

On her knees, she melted like ice under the sun. It was the first time she took his name so loud that time stopped. All these years when she thought he'd forgotten her, he was going through all of this just because of those silly things she said over the call.

His sister picked her up and said, he has left this note for you:

'Smile, and move on. Maybe you've found someone you deserve. I hope he cares for you more than how much you care for me right now. You said you didn't love me. I didn't believe you. I knew we'd meet, it's just that you took a little longer. Welcome back, now I want you to move on.

PS: See you in the next life, after 60-80 years. In just a few moments, these people will burn me. I'll turn into ashes. Yes, we will meet soon in the next life. A life where I'd be the guy, and you'd be my girl. I'm sure you'd do a better job than me. Love you, eternal.'

title: Fuck You
text:
The end.

You might think that's a bad word to start a sentence with, but that's what it is. The end.

I don't know how to filter my words the way you filter your pictures, so I'm going to be very candid and upfront here and this time, without a sorry, because you've earned this shit and I'm giving it back to you.

So darling, thank you for teaching me the reality of relationships that I have now accepted. They only have two outcomes, either it works out or it fucking doesn't.

Thank you, because I learned it's the lessons you learn from the wrong ones that live on forever. These lessons guide you to the next person, or maybe the right one.

But I also want to say fuck you, because you ruined my favorite songs forever.

We're not talking to each other and I don't care, but I'll keep you forever in the only picture of us we have, so thank you for that photo. It means a lot to me, it was the day when we said those words to each other.

But fuck you, I don't believe in those words anymore.

Thank you for those late night conversations but fuck you, for doing it with every other guy you met.

Thank you, without you, the people who love me wouldn't have spent hours of their time with me reminding that it's okay to be broken by someone you blind-trusted.

Fuck you, I can't even trust them anymore.

Thank you for making me a poet, but fuck you for that kiss.

Thank you for giving me some of the best memories that I'll cherish all my life, but fuck you for making me miss them alone.

Thank you for loving me, but fuck you for making me hate myself.

Thank you for that crimson love, but fuck you that people still notice it in my eyes.

Curled up in my covers I might miss you again, yet fuck you, goodbye.

Thank you for teaching me this fancy 'fuck you' word, but fuck you, I'm giving it all back.

Be guilty, your game was filthy.
Be surprised, I survived.

From here, it'll not be about you anymore.

Thank you, n Love you

P.S. say hello to your mother for me, she loved me like a son.

The Beginning.
